career_ladder.note: Judicial officers in Uttar Pradesh are governed by the Uttar Pradesh Judicial Service Rules, 2001 and the Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) uniform pay matrix as mandated by the Supreme Court of India in All India Judges Association v. Union of India. Officers enjoy Assured Career Progression (ACP) at 5-year intervals even if cadre vacancies for promotional posts are awaiting availability.

exam_scheme.note: Examination is conducted in three successive stages: Preliminary Examination (Objective, screening only), Main Examination (Conventional descriptive written), and Viva-Voce (Personality Test). Language papers were separated into English (100 marks) and Hindi (100 marks) under amended UP Judicial Service Rules.

financial_package.note: Judicial officers in UP are paid in accordance with the Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) uniform pay scale accepted by the Supreme Court of India in All India Judges Association v. Union of India. Civil Judge (Junior Division) starts at SNJPC Level J-1 with entry basic pay of ₹77,840.
financial_package.pay_source_label: Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) Report & Supreme Court of India Order in WP(C) No. 643/2015
financial_package.estimate_note: Calculated based on SNJPC J-1 entry basic pay of ₹77,840 at 58% Dearness Allowance (effective 1 Jul 2025), plus judicial allowances (sumptuary allowance ₹1,500, robe allowance, medical allowance, transport allowance) and HRA ranging from 10% to 30% depending on posting district in Uttar Pradesh.
official_perks: Official rent-free residential bungalow / government accommodation designated for judicial officers
Official staff (Orderly, Peon, and Camp Office Clerk / Stenographer)
Official vehicle with driver / conveyance facility for official duty
Sumptuary Allowance and Robe Allowance as per SNJPC recommendations
Full medical reimbursement for self and dependent family members
Leave Travel Concession (LTC) and Home Travel Concession

competition_benchmarks.note: Applicant, preliminary appearance, Mains shortlist, and final vacancy statistics are drawn from official UPPSC press releases and notifications for Advt. No. A-5/E-1/2022 and Advt. No. A-3/E-1/2018.

years.source_label: UPPSC Advt. No. A-5/E-1/2022 Notification & Press Release: 303 vacancies for Civil Judge (Junior Division); 79,565 applicants registered, 50,837 appeared in Prelims, 3,145 qualified for Mains, 959 appeared in Viva-Voce.
UPPSC Advt. No. A-3/E-1/2018 Notification & Final Result: 610 vacancies; 64,591 applicants registered, 5,795 shortlisted for Mains.
